name: fetch keepalive
plain: A fetch flag that lets the request finish after the page is gone.
meaning: Replaces sendBeacon when a site needs custom headers or methods on exit. The browser holds the request open past unload, with the same 64 KiB cap. Firefox shipped it in version 133 (Nov 2024).

access.persistence: Until the request completes or fails
access.revocation: Clear site data, browser privacy settings

limits.headline: Can finish sending a request after you leave or close the page
limits.user_action: Nothing. It happens when you close or leave a page that has a pending report
can: Complete a request that was started before you left
Send a last report about the visit
Send a small amount of data even as the page unloads
cannot: Send a large amount of data, since there is a small size limit
Keep running for long after the page is gone
Run if the browser or a blocker stops the request
Show you a prompt or any sign
limits.reach_label: A final report, as you leave

story.what_it_is: A flag that lets a web request finish even if you close the page.

marketing.name: Request keepalive
marketing.pitch: Developer docs say keepalive lets a request outlive the page, so a final report can go out as you leave.

story.for_you: You never see it. You close a tab or click away, and the page quietly sends one last note that finishes after the page is gone. It might be your time on page or a saved draft.
story.for_makers: Sites need a way to report at exit, when normal requests are cancelled. Keepalive allows custom headers and methods, which sendBeacon does not. The 64 KiB cap limits how much can go.

use_cases.example: A news site reports how long you read and how far you scrolled as you close the article.
A browser game sends your final score or a session end event when you close the tab, so progress is not lost.
An online editor sends a last autosave while you close the tab, so your last words are saved.
A video site sends your watch position when you leave, so the next visit resumes at the same moment.
A fraud tool sends a final batch of mouse and typing data when you leave a checkout page.
An ad tag sends a last viewability report that says how long the ad was on screen.

risks: Can send data as you leave

technical_bounds: About 64 KiB total in flight per page
Not available with all request modes
